experiment: NES gradient-free (forward-only) black-box attack ceiling check vs CoGEO, held-out rank-lift
anchor: product_title (anchor-decoupled; eval query held out, never used in NES optimization)
pool: 491-ASIN distractor pool == CoGEO eval pool (non-attacked ASINs are verbatim original copies)
scoring_note: Both NES and CoGEO scored by the SAME evaluator code/rank_eval_nes.py (GPU-preproc reimpl of eval_harness rank math). Cross-checked on this 120-subset: rank_eval_nes CoGEO rank_lift=14.258 matches eval_harness CoGEO rank_lift=14.258 exactly; on full 500 the GPU-vs-CPU preproc gives delta 0.03061 vs harness 0.03145.
interpretation: At a 2000 forward-query/image budget on the SAME 120 cohort-balanced pairs (E/S/C/I=30) and SAME 491-ASIN pool, both NES and CoGEO scored by the identical evaluator (rank_eval_nes.py): gradient-free NES reaches only 22.8% of CoGEO held-out rank-lift (3.05 vs 13.39) and 48.8% of CoGEO held-out delta (0.01510 vs 0.03094). Paired Wilcoxon two-sided: rank_lift p=4.05e-04, delta p=2.81e-10 -> CoGEO significantly exceeds NES on both; one-sided greater(NES>CoGEO) p~1.0 (no evidence NES wins). NES gain is genuine (100% of images raised title-anchor cosine, mean +0.0639, all within eps=16/255, linf_max=16). Conclusion: a pure gradient-free NES black-box attack does NOT reach the CoGEO ceiling at 2000 queries/image; CoGEO retains a large (~4.7x rank-lift, ~2x delta), statistically significant held-out advantage.
